concept: RPA is software that operates other software through screens, clicks, typing and copying to perform rule-based repetitive digital work. It is not a physical robot, artificial intelligence by itself, a system replacement, or a cure for a poor process.
rules: Standard RPA follows developer-written rules and does not learn or infer
RPA works on top of existing ERP, email and web systems
common_errors: Automating an inefficient process without redesign

concept: Manual work has no build cost but is slow and error-prone; Excel macros are cheap but usually stay inside one application; system integration is fast and reliable but needs an interface and high development effort; RPA has wider reach and medium effort but is vulnerable to UI changes; replacing a system has the highest cost, time and disruption.

Attended robots run on an employee desktop on demand; unattended robots run on a server or VM from a schedule, queue or event. Design builds workflows, Execute runs them, and Orchestrate deploys, schedules, stores credentials, manages queues and logs.
rules: Attended licensing is normally per user and unattended licensing per robot

concept: A UiPath automation consists of a trigger, ordered activities, data carried by variables and arguments, selectors for identifying UI elements, exception handling and logging. An anchor is a stable UI landmark used to locate a target whose ID or position is not reliable.
rules: Production workflows require exception handling and logging
Selectors can break after UI, resolution, language or dialog changes
common_errors: Omitting logging or a fallback path
exercise_connection: Use Application/Browser, Type Into, two Click activities and Extract Table Data on the Streamlit app

concept: The seven-step delivery lifecycle is Identify, Assess, Design, Build, Test, Deploy and Sustain. Sustain is ongoing monitoring, maintenance and improvement, not an optional post-project activity.

A strong automation candidate has high volume, rule-based decisions, structured digital input, a stable process, stable systems and a low exception rate. Three or four positive criteria are generally enough to continue assessment. Judgement, frequent change, paper or free text, low volume, unstable systems and imminent replacement are warning signs.

RPA can improve speed, consistency, peak capacity, traceability and redeployment without changing an ERP. Main risks are UI fragility, maintenance cost, lack of judgement, retained inefficiency, understated licence/support cost and staff resistance. Controls include a named account, least privilege, segregation of duties, version/change control, monitoring and a tested manual fallback.

Task automation uses fixed rules; intelligent automation combines RPA with document understanding or machine learning; agentic automation lets an agent plan and adapt while RPA performs repeatable execution. Agents complement rather than replace rule-based robots.

Read Range creates a DataTable copy in robot memory, not a live link to Google Sheets. Changes to the copy reach the sheet only after an explicit write-back. Data rows use zero-based indexes and the header row is represented by column names, not a data row.
rules: Do not treat the header as data

concept: For Each Row in Spreadsheet exposes the current row and its fields. Has headers=True treats the first row as column names; Has headers=False treats it as data. Values can be accessed by a column name or index.
exercise_connection: Read account details with For Each Row in Spreadsheet and validate Email and First name

concept: Write-back modes include Overwrite, Append and Insert. When a sheet has headers, CurrentRowIndex 0 maps to physical spreadsheet Row 2, so a status cell uses CurrentRowIndex + 2. This prevents overwriting headers or addressing Row 0.
common_errors: Editing the DataTable without writing it back

concept: Regular expressions validate a complete shape when anchored with ^ and $. In the course email pattern ^[\w\.]+@\w+\.\w+$, \w is a word character, + means one or more, and \. means a literal dot. A bare dot means any character.
rules: The ^ and $ anchors require the whole input string to match this course pattern
This is a simplified teaching pattern; matching it is not the same as accepting every syntactically valid real-world email address

concept: AND requires every condition to be true; OR requires at least one condition to be true. The exercise uses Regex.IsMatch(Email, pattern) is true AND First name is not empty, then sets status_value to Passed or Failed and writes it outside the If block.

Supplier invoices can contain the same business fields in different page locations. A machine-learning document model reads field meaning rather than fixed coordinates and maps varied layouts into one consistent spreadsheet schema.

A custom document model is built by collecting representative documents, labelling fields, training, and evaluating on unseen documents. UiPath pre-trained models have already completed that work for common document types such as invoices and receipts, but extracted values still need validation.

For invoice extraction, set Input to CurrentItem from the PDF loop, Project to Predefined, Extractor to Invoices and Output to documentData. Generate Data Type=True enables typed dot notation; Auto-validation is off by default and a 3600-second timeout is the safe exercise default.
exercise_connection: For Each File or Folder filtered to PDF → Extract Document Data

concept: Document Understanding follows Digitise, Classify, Extract, Validate and Export. OCR happens during Digitise for scans; validation can use confidence thresholds, business rules or a human; export writes the accepted values to a target system such as Google Sheets.

Document Data contains header fields such as VendorName, InvoiceNumber and InvoiceDate plus an Items table. Each field exposes Value and Confidence. Confidence helps route work but a high score does not prove correctness; arithmetic and business checks are still needed.

Header values are written once per invoice, while line items require an inner For Each over documentData.Data.Items. The list Index is zero-based but spreadsheet rows start at 1, so CurrentRowNumber = Index + 1 and item columns are addressed as D, E, F and G plus that row number.
common_errors: Using one loop for both PDFs and line items
Overwriting line items by using a fixed cell
Leaving header fields blank on appended rows

concept: Predefined models supply a fixed published field list and are best for common document types such as invoices. Generative Predefined models let the developer define field names and instructions for uncommon documents, but are slower, metered differently and subject to field and response limits.

Straight-through processing is appropriate only when required fields pass confidence and arithmetic/business checks. A low-confidence or failed-rule document becomes a human-in-the-loop validation task in Action Center; human corrections are useful labelled data for improving the process.

Agentic automation gives a language model a goal, instructions, context, tools and an output contract. The model chooses what to call at runtime, while RPA activities still read sheets, update records and send messages.

The four parts are Instructions (system prompt), Context (user prompt and current data), Tools (callable workflows or services), and Output (the required response format). A wrong result on every row suggests the system prompt; a wrong result on some rows suggests the user prompt or source data.

Appointment Reply Agent Solution contains an Appointment Reply Workflow, an Agent and an Appointment Check Workflow. The reply workflow passes EmailBody and EmailAddress to the agent; the agent selects Check, Change or Cancel and fills the tool's In arguments; the tool returns Out_ProcessReturn.

The appointment tool matches CurrentRow.Name to In_CustomerName, switches on In_CustomerRequest, returns the date for Check, writes In_CustomerDate to column B at CurrentRowIndex + 2 for Change, and deletes the matching row at CurrentRowIndex + 1 for Cancel. If no row matches, it returns Appointment not found.

The agent drafts the response, but the fixed RPA workflow performs Send Email through the Google Workspace connection. Keeping the irreversible send outside the agent preserves a deterministic control point and auditability.

The eight phases are Process Identification, Assessment and Redesign, Tool and Vendor Selection, Solution Design, Development, Testing, Deployment and Hypercare, and Maintenance and CoE. Each phase has inputs, activities, artefacts and an exit gate.

Assessment documents the as-is process and to-be redesign. Solution Design produces a signed-off PDD, SDD and exception matrix covering scope, workflow architecture, applications, data, logging, error handling and escalation before development starts.

Development should use a separate environment, modular workflows, logging, exception handling, version control and peer review. Testing progresses from unit tests to end-to-end system tests and business UAT, including bad inputs, destructive tests, back-testing and forward-testing.

Production release needs a rollback plan, round-the-clock hypercare and a manual Plan B. Maintenance logs changes, fixes in development, retests and redeploys. A Centre of Excellence governs standards, reusable components, monitoring and the automation pipeline.

The Meridian expense-claims case requires multi-channel intake, employee and cost-centre checks, receipt matching, policy and approval validation, GST treatment, SAP posting, SharePoint filing and status tracking. Key constraints are Singapore data residency, immutable audit trails, segregation of duties, no direct SAP database writes, retirement of Access, a S$120,000 year-one cap and five-month go-live.
rules: P-01 claims within 60 days or Regional Director approval
P-06 items above S$300 need pre-approval
P-07 approval level is based on total claim amount
P-08 GST recovery needs a valid tax invoice
P-11 no self or reciprocal approval
P-12 terminated employees go to Claims Supervisor
